issues.title: Capability work is missing from the attempt budget
issues.problem: The attempt resource receipt measures the provider process. It does not exclusively own and account for all capability, browser, adapter, and completion work that Buster launches.
issues.impact: A cheap provider can report low resource usage while its other local work exceeds the claimed CPU, memory or process budget.
issues.current_state: Core now performs early and final resource observations. runner.measure still reads instance.resources(); moving the observation later does not create exclusive whole-attempt ownership. Related locally closed Prism/Core findings are not reopened. Durable fixture readiness/control, separate readiness/completion promises, a bounded fourth process pipe and native launcher ownership primitives exist as locally tested building blocks. The production runner still constructs LocalWorkerRuntime; the native lifetime API is not its production execution path.
remaining_work: Integrate durable attempt/claim-bound local execution ownership across Core and Buster, including provider work, parent capability execution, browser/command children, adapters, evidence and finalization.

Define aggregate measurement and hard budget enforcement. Distinguish cumulative CPU from CPU rate and processes from cgroup tasks. Required missing observations must fail. Declare remote BuildKit/Kubernetes work separately.
Preserve retained fixtures through durable ownership transfer, fences and crash recovery; coordinate with PCR-BUSTER-ENGINE-004.

Connect the actual Buster attempt host, restricted role-specific launch policy/broker and durable fixture lifetime to the runner. Keep broker and capability work inside the attempt scope. After the verified cutover remove the superseded executable runner, file-capability launch and sampling paths; retain no executable fallback.
reproduction: Run the original provider in an actual delegated cgroup. Keep its own load small and launch two real capability children whose combined load exceeds the attempt budget although individual limits pass.

Put load separately in the report adapter and finalization. Compare the original receipt and terminal state with aggregate counters; unrelated concurrent service work must not be charged to this attempt.
Exercise short-lived children, descendants surviving their leader, missing counters, cancellation and drain failure. Fake cgroup files are not positive containment evidence.
acceptance_criteria: Every claimed local phase has exclusive ownership or demonstrably non-overlapping equivalent accounting.
Aggregate overrun or missing required observations prevent completed; successful drain leaves no local work running.
Original Core/Buster claim, timeout, fixture and evidence guarantees remain covered.

Fixture readiness is journaled before dependency acknowledgement, teardown fences acknowledgement races, and only the original Core terminal journal seals completion. Historical readiness cannot authorize new dependents.
issues.live_validation: Actual delegated cgroups and real providers/browsers are required. Acceptance in the deployed worker container is separate.

issues.title: Restarted terminal jobs retain source workspaces without a durable quiescence proof
issues.problem: After a worker or host crash there is no durable proof that every process belonging to a job has stopped. Source and working directories therefore remain retained.
issues.impact: Repeated interrupted jobs can consume disk and quotas. Deleting from terminal metadata alone could remove inputs still used by live descendants.
issues.current_state: Normal confirmed execution cleans inputs. Durable status write and read failures stop admission; shutdown waits for pending admission writes. recover() explicitly retains inputs because a terminal record does not prove orphan quiescence.
remaining_work: Publish durable job/attempt/claim ownership before launch and include capability children, adapters and retained fixtures.
On restart reconcile the exact fenced owner and require authoritative complete termination. Preserve and diagnose unknown ownership instead of guessing.
Authorize the existing narrow idempotent input cleanup only after that proof; preserve valid result, evidence and log receipts.
reproduction: Crash and restart the original worker with a live provider plus actual capability/adapter children. Distinguish leader death from complete process termination.
Exercise crash windows around ownership publication, drain and file removal; reused or namespace-mismatched PIDs must never authorize cleanup.
Read completed/failed/cancelled job receipts and retained-fixture transitions after restart.
acceptance_criteria: No active or uncertain owner loses its inputs.
After complete quiescence is proved, only authorized inputs are removed; repeated recovery is safe.
Real quota release and retained result/evidence access are demonstrated on original jobs.
issues.live_validation: Native crash and containment tests are required. Log retention and external demo lifetime are independent of source-workspace cleanup.

issues.title: Confirmed run history lacks complete connected retirement
issues.problem: Confirmed history still lacks a complete release protocol understood by every reader and component that can reopen, accept or replay it.
issues.impact: Partial compaction can leave record, metadata, evidence and blob quotas exhausted. Uncoordinated deletion could lose evidence or protection against repeated external actions.
issues.current_state: Telemetry, admission, imported attempt results, redundant dispatch archive copies and causal operator projections have bounded implementations and local evidence. They do not remove all job counts, evidence objects or shared blobs. The dispatch projection has a real one-POST replay result while retaining logical job, receipt and source blob. Its native provider execution failed; that failure does not invalidate the bounded storage transition or prove successful native execution.
remaining_work: Inventory active/completed owners, all current reopen/accept/read/replay consumers and shared references.
Implement explicit manual release with durable consumer completion and required idempotency/uncertainty tombstones, atomically across those consumers. Keep every still-required reference resolvable.
Release actual byte and record quotas rather than moving data into unaccounted sidecars. D07 does not permit automatic age-based log deletion.
reproduction: Use small real store quotas with active, waiting and completed runs and shared artifacts; measure actual bytes and entries before/after authorized release.
Replay old deliveries after restart and exercise competing writers and SIGKILL between durable transitions.
Use original result, evidence, artifact and operator readers on retired and deliberately retained history.
acceptance_criteria: Only authorized and fully confirmed history is released; active and uncertain work remains intact.
Released capacity admits new actual writes. Replays do not repeat an external action or fabricate delivery outcomes.
All affected consumers understand the same retirement state and retain the existing projection guarantees.
issues.live_validation: Original local store/process tests can close this implementation scope. Cleanup of real user data remains a separate operational action.

reproduction: Using the real runtime image, execute two distinct build jobs and negatively test unauthorized process visibility, signals and background processes surviving job completion.

issues.title: Continuous GitOps health compares a branch name with resolved commit IDs

issues.impact: An actually synchronized healthy runtime child reporting its SHA can remain Progressing in the app-of-apps gate and block later waves. This is a source-confirmed mismatch, not an observed live outage.
issues.current_state: Source inspection identified the mismatch in integrated main. Existing health tests cover exact commit pins, stale-operation rejection and separate observed platform mode, but contain no positive continuous main-with-resolved-SHA case.

issues.title: Accepted no-decay preference contract conflicts with automatic 180-day decay
issues.problem: The accepted prism-preference-learning-v1 document explicitly excludes automatic time decay, while projectPreferences computes score * 0.5^(ageDays/180) and createPreferenceGeneration persists policyVersion=prism.preferences.v1.decay180-project-override.
issues.impact: Readers cannot determine whether preferences should remain stable with age or weaken automatically. Different contract interpretations can produce different effective preferences for the same event history.
issues.current_state: Both current implementation files and the accepted no-decay statements were inspected at the source baseline. Tests explicitly cover decay and snapshot policy identity. No authoritative approval superseding the no-decay rule was identified in this bounded reconciliation; that approval state remains unknown rather than inferred from code.
remaining_work: Resolve the contract explicitly: retain the accepted no-decay rule or document an approved replacement specifying the intended temporal policy.

Align implementation, policyVersion, documentation and regression expectations with that decision. Preserve event provenance, retraction, referenceTime, project-over-personal behavior and deterministic snapshot replay; do not silently reinterpret historical snapshots.
reproduction: Inspect docs/architecture/prism-preference-learning-v1.md. V1 excludes automatic time decay in the opening scope and time-handling section. Compare skills/prism/preferences/index.ts projectPreferences and skills/prism/control/preference-snapshot.ts.

Use one valid selected event with a single trait and evaluate the original projector at its last evidence time and 180 days later. Current arithmetic yields score1/effectiveScore1, then score1/effectiveScore0.5. Preserve user and project context with all required event fields. The source inspection did not execute the probe.

Existing regression entry points: skills/prism/tests/quality.test.mts (preference projections decay and remain retractable) and skills/prism/tests/control-generation-http.test.mts (persisted decay policy identity).

issues.title: Uncertain external effects have no supported reconciliation and result-import operation
issues.problem: Effect recovery correctly stops when an external service accepts a request without returning a trustworthy receipt. It also stops when a receipt exists without terminal attempt evidence. The current platform supplies no supported operation that records reconciliation and imports the authoritative result.
issues.impact: An operator can identify an uncertain effect but cannot continue the run through a documented, validated state transition. Blind retry can duplicate an external mutation, while journal editing would bypass lifecycle authority.
issues.current_state: Source tracing followed the recovery guard through normal execution and administrative retry. Both paths stop on unresolved external outcomes. The effectful guide states this limit and does not invent a continuation command.
remaining_work: Define a versioned reconciliation request and result contract with actor identity, effect identity, evidence, idempotency and authorization.
Implement one Core-owned operation that records the decision and imports or compensates the result without editing journals.
Add failure, duplicate, cancellation, restart and audit tests, then document the supported operator and extension behavior.
reproduction: Run the persistent external-effect recovery tests in the verification record.
Create an accepted external effect without a receipt, then attempt normal resume and administrative retry. Observe that both paths return the unresolved-outcome guard.
Inspect skills/nova/core/execution/effect-recovery.ts, engine-run.ts and engine-admin.ts. Confirm that no supported reconciliation import operation follows the stop.
acceptance_criteria: An authorized operator can reconcile one uncertain effect through a supported API without direct journal changes.
The operation rejects mismatched effect, attempt, actor and evidence identities and remains idempotent after restart.
The effectful extension guide includes the exact operation, observations, failure paths and retained evidence.
issues.live_validation: Local contract and restart tests can prove the state transition. A real external service remains a separate live acceptance exercise.

evidence.assessment: Independent source trace and local recovery exercises; no reconciliation implementation was added.
evidence.prior_verification: The review confirmed that normal, retry and remediation paths preserve the recovery stop.

sources.scope: The recovery guard rejects unresolved and externally incomplete effects.

issues.title: Prism OpenClaw tools lack general payload and request-lifetime limits
issues.problem: The Prism OpenClaw extension bounds the number of designs but does not define general text or document size limits. Its HTTP request also has no explicit timeout or cancellation signal.
issues.impact: A large request or stalled Prism control connection can retain host resources for an undefined period. Extension authors cannot copy a complete bounded-call pattern from this package.
issues.current_state: The guide no longer describes the existing Prism tools as fully bounded. It distinguishes requirements for a new extension from behavior that Prism currently implements.
remaining_work: Approve explicit request-size, text-size and document-size limits for both Prism tools.
Add an explicit timeout and cancellation propagation contract to the HTTP call.
Test boundary values, cancellation, timeout, host registration and error mapping, then update the package page.
reproduction: Inspect skills/prism/openclaw-plugin/index.mjs and identify the design-count constraint.
Confirm that the parameter schemas do not set complete text/document bounds and that the fetch call has no timeout or cancellation signal.
Run the current registration tests and observe that they check names and design count, not a real host request lifetime.
acceptance_criteria: Approved schemas bound all request-controlled payloads or record a justified alternative resource boundary.
The client enforces a documented timeout and propagates cancellation without committing a partial revision.
Tests exercise limits and real host registration, and the host-extension guide states the verified behavior.
issues.live_validation: Local schema and cancellation tests are required first. A real OpenClaw-to-Prism call remains separate live evidence.

evidence.assessment: Independent source and registration-test inspection; no product implementation changed.
